title: Graceful pin deprecations and multi-tier failover for pinned model versions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers can pin exact model versions for deterministic outputs, but pins make it hard to maintain SLOs when a specific version is unavailable (capacity, regional outage, deprecated kernel). We need a predictable, auditable fallback policy for pinned versions that preserves customer intent where possible, minimizes user-visible regressions, and gives operators safe levers to keep traffic flowing.

Goals: Provide a deterministic fallback order and deprecation flow for pinned versions; expose opt-in controls to customers (strict pin vs. allowed soft fallbacks); surface events and audits in Console; ensure telemetry captures fallback reason and quality deltas; implement server-side safeguards to prevent silent quality regressions or security issues.

Scope: Design and implement control-plane policy + runtime routing changes to support: (1) region failover when a pinned version's region capacity is down, (2) model-variant fallback (e.g., float32 -> int8/quantized -> distilled variant) when an exact version is unavailable, (3) deprecation windows with automated migration suggestions, and (4) an API/Console UI for pin policy flags (strict|graceful|notify-only).

Key design decisions made so far: (A) Fallback ordering will be explicit and deterministic: same-version same-region -> same-version other-region (configurable latency budget) -> compatible-variant same-region -> compatible-variant other-region. (B) We will support two pin modes: strict (no fallback permitted) and graceful (fallbacks allowed following the order). Customers default to graceful unless they explicitly choose strict. (C) Deprecation is policy-driven: model owners set a deprecation_date and a suggested migration target; customers with pinned versions receive staged notifications (30d/14d/7d/1d) and an optional auto-migrate window that only triggers if the customer's pin is in graceful mode and service is degraded.

Trade-offs: Strict pins preserve exact behavior at the cost of availability; graceful mode reduces downtime but may change generation characteristics. We decided to prioritize availability for most customers by default (graceful), while exposing strict for compliance use cases. We also avoid automatic migration for strict pins to honor determinism.

Operational safeguards: Telemetry will report fallback events with tags: fallback_type, from_version, to_version, region_from, region_to, latency_delta, token_cost_delta, evaluation_quality_delta (if eval set available). Rollbacks and audit logs will be preserved. Fallbacks that increase error-rate or quality regression beyond configured thresholds will auto-abort and route to a safe degraded path (e.g., same model family but at lower throughput with operator paging).

Open questions: 1) How aggressive should cross-region fallback latency budget be by default? 2) Should we allow cross-architecture fallbacks (e.g., Llama2 -> open-compat) or restrict to verified compatible variants? 3) UI language for deprecation notifications to enterprise customers.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (API + control plane): extend model catalog schema to capture deprecation_date, suggested_migration, verified_variants, and pin_policy flags. Add audit events and notification hooks. Phase 2 (runtime): implement deterministic routing policy in the routing layer and fallback admission checks with thresholds. Phase 3 (console + docs): Console toggles per-customer and per-route, migration suggestions, and changelog for deprecations. Phase 4 (QA + rollout): internal dogfood -> opt-in beta customers -> GA.

References and artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Graceful+Pin+Fallbacks , PR proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234 , eval harness draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X_example_link

Notes for engineers: implement extensive unit tests for fallback ordering, and e2e tests simulating region outage and variant-unavailability. Add synthetic traffic tests to ensure SLOs meet expectations under fallback scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane model metadata extended to include deprecation_date, suggested_migration, verified_variants, and pin_policy
API accepts pin_policy (strict|graceful|notify-only) on route-level and account-level pins
Runtime implements deterministic fallback ordering and records fallback events with required telemetry fields
Console surfaces pin policy, deprecation timelines, and one-click suggested migrations for graceful pins
Automated notifications (30/14/7/1 days) are sent for deprecations to pinned customers
E2E test simulating region outage results in failover according to configured latency budget for graceful pins
Strict pins guarantee no automatic migration; requests return 409 with actionable message when pinned version unavailable
Fallbacks that exceed configured quality regression thresholds trigger automatic abort and create an incident ticket
